description.narrative: KSP aims to support sustainable urban development in Kenya primarily through an exchange of expertise, knowledge and experiences between Kenyan and Swedish actors. It will implement the Swedish inspired concept for urban sustainability - Symbiocity Approach – which has also been successfully implemented with modification in various countries in the world. The project will be anchored at the Council of Governors, which will coordinate the project on behalf of counties. The Swedish Association and Regions (SALAR) will provide technical assistance and linkages with Swedish actors based on experience gained implementing similar projects across the world. In addition to strengthening the coordination role of the CoG, the project will build sustainable urban development planning capacity within the CoG and counties. It will also pilot interventions in at least 7 counties using the Symbiocity approach. Based on lessons learnt from the pilots, the project will expand capacity building activities to all the 47 counties. In the process, the project will build the institutional capacity of CoG, strengthen counties’ capacity for planning and implementing project using a sustainability perspective and improve access to infrastructure and services in selected counties. Ultimately, it is expected that the project will contribute to improved conditions for urban residents in Kenya.

Kenya SymbioCity Programmet (KSP) syftar till att stödja hållbar urban utveckling i Kenya, huvud-sakligen genom att kenyanska och svenska aktörer utbyter expertis, kunskaper och erfaren¬heter. Det är det svenskinspirerade konceptet för urban hållbarhet – SymbioCity – som ska genomföras, och som i olika modifierade former framgångsrikt genomförts i flera länder runt om i världen. Projektet kommer att genomföras tillsammans med Council of Governors (CoG, som är de lokala regeringschefernas högsta råd och en officiell lagstiftad institution som representerar samtliga 47 Länsregeringar), som ska koordinera projektet för och med länsregeringarna, genom CoG:s specifika projektkontor (PIU) och genom Kommittén för Urban Utveckling på CoG. Projektkontoret kommer att hantera finansiellt och tekninskt stöd till länen, men inte kanalisera medel vidare till länen i denna första insatsperiod. Sveriges Kommuner och Landsting (SKL) kommer att bidra med teknisk assistans till CoG och länen och dessutom förmedla kontakter med svenska aktörer utifrån erfarenheter från genomföranden av liknande projekt runtom i världen. Utöver att stärka CoG:s koordinerande roll kommer projektet att leda till att det byggs upp planeringskapacitet för en hållbar urban utveckling vid CoG och hos länsregeringarna (som alla är representerade genom CoG). Pilotprojekt som utgår från förhållningssättet SymbioCity kommer att genomföras i minst sju regioner. Utifrån de lärdomar som dras av pilotprojekten kommer det sedan att genomföras kapacitetsuppbyggande aktiviteter i alla de 47 regionerna. Under processen kommer det att byggas upp institutionell kapacitet hos CoG, samtidigt som kapaciteten för att - utifrån ett hållbarhets¬perspektiv - planera och genomföra projekt kommer att stärkas, samt att tillgången till infrastruktur och tjänster i de utvalda regionerna ökar. Slutligen förväntas projektet bidra till förbättrade levnadsvillkor och möjligheter för urbana invånare i Kenya.

The overall goal of the programme was to contribute to "Inclusive, innovative and sustainable urban development planning in Kenya". The intermediary programme objective was "Urban development stakeholders have increased capacity and ability to guide Kenyan urban development in a more sustainable direction". Supporting the intermediary programme objective were four objectives: 1) CoG is set up to be responsive to counties needs and support urban planning, management and development: This would be achieved through institutional development activities and knowledge transfer from the experienced SALAR. A particular focus was the creation and or strengthening of a technical unit to support the Urban Development Committee. 2) Local stakeholders in seven counties plan, manage and develop their localities with a sustainable perspective: This would be achieved through the piloting of the SymbioCity Approach in a real urban local setting, leading to a needs analysis through the urban sustainability review process and development of urban visions to be taken further by the county. Piloting of urban improvements according to SymbioCity approach principles was also included in this objective. 3) MoLHUD/UDD and CoG have increased capacity to support urban planning, management and development in counties: This entailed institutional development activities coupled with improved collaboration between MoLHUD and CoG for supporting sustainable urban planning, development and management, in line with the national urban development policy. 4) Kenya SymbioCity Programme experiences shared among counties and urban development stakeholders to stimulate cross fertilization and networking: This objective would be achieved through the networking and interaction with other projects and organisations, which would help disseminate SymbioCity expertise and experience.

description.narrative:
Summary of results Programme Objective 1: CoG has improved capacity to be responsive to counties' needs and to support urban planning, management and development It is worth noting however that based on the first amendment to the specific agreement between the National Treasury and the Embassy of Sweden which was informed by the midterm review of the programme, programme objective 1 continued to receive minimal attention from the project resources both financial and human resources. The programme was however able to inspire the Council of Governors to establish a technical support team within the secretariat to support the Land, Planning and Urban Development Committee. At the programme inception the Council did not have a technical officer with planning background. The absorption of the Project Manager and two other staff (Finance Officer and the Procurement Officer) is critical in sustaining the capacity developed through the programme and further replication of the SymbioCity Approach.
Programme objective 2: Strategic and systematic knowledge management established at CoG This strategy envisaged a strategic and systematic knowledge management established at the Council of Governors. This would be achieved through consultations with representatives of county governments on current issues on the urban agenda and the development and use of the SymbioCity Kenya Programme resources. During the programme period, the Council of Governors in partnership with SALAR and other stakeholders through the Kenya SymbioCity Programme contributed to the realization of this strategy through the following activities: Development of the Planning our towns, Tool Kit for Sustainable Urban Development. During the programme period the Kenya SymbioCity programme continued to disseminate the tool kit to guide integrated development planning in line with the SymbioCity Kenya Principles amongst the counties and other stakeholders. The tool kit was widely disseminated amongst counties, cities, municipalities and towns amongst other stakeholders and currently has become a reference point in the development of integrated development plans for Kenyan Municipalities. So far Kitui Municipality which hosts one of the SymbioCity pilot towns Kwa Vonza utilized this toolkit on the development of their integrated development plan.
Quick Wins (selection) Nakuru County During the preparation of the Urban Sustainability Review for Njoro, certain challenges had been identified. Water (i.e. domestic water & storm water) was identified as a major challenge. With the quick win and in readiness for implementation of the change project, certain activities needed to be undertaken as quick wins they included: 1. Hydrogeological (Geotechnical Survey) Study to establish the drilling site and its characteristics in readiness for the drilling of borehole in the change project which was financed by the County Government of Nakuru 2. Jewatho Settlement Storm Water Drainage Design in readiness for the storm water drainage works in the change project which was funded by the programme. All these activities had been executed as they formed basis for the change projects.
Kakamega County In Kakamega County the quick win project was conceptualized by the community as an urban project which could be implemented within a short period of time and create a big impact to the public. The quick win in Butere included: 1. Survey and beaconing of public land (Butere EcoPark) for securing and later development through change project and other County Interventions 2. Fencing of the project site to prevent encroachment 3. Construction of refuse chambers in Sabatia Market and Lower Butere Market. 4. Earthworks (ground levelling) at Butere EcoPark site. (This was cofunded by the County Government at a cost of two million Kenya Shillings). All the above components of the project have since been completed.
TransNzoia County In TransNzoia, the quick win focused on solid waste management as well as public space. This was achieved through: 1. Installation of street benches 2. Single Waste bins 3. Double waste bins 4. Tree Planting 5. Procurement of Bulk bins All the above activities were implemented as envisioned.
Change Projects (selection) Nakuru County Nakuru change project was being implemented in Jewathu Settlement within Njoro sub County in Nakuru County. The area has a high population of Njoro residents but with constrained resources. Access to clean water and poor drainage were the top priority issues that were identified through the urban sustainably review process and therefore the Change project was designed to address these two concerns. Improved access to clean and safe water for Jewathu residents was to be realized through the construction of a borehole to serve the people of Jewathu. Before the drilling of the borehole the county government committed to undertake a hydrogeological survey within Njoro Township Integrated Primary School which was undertaken by the countys department of water in October 2019. The survey identified the most suitable site to drill the borehole. After the hydrogeological survey the project financed the drilling of the borehole, thereafter water samples were taken to national government laboratories for water quality test which confirmed that the water was fit for consumption. The project benefits 2000 households within Njoro Township. Improved storm water infrastructure and drainage system was to be realized through the implementation of the drainage design developed during the quick win period. As at the end of the programme the County Government of Nakuru had completed the drainage System as envisaged. The Council of Governors engaged with the County Government of Nakuru which committed to allocate resources for regular operations and maintenance.
Kisumu County Kisumu change project was implemented in Ahero town a secondary town near Kisumu City. During the urban sustainability review process, stakeholders in Ahero identified the following sustainability challenges 1. Lack of modern sanitary facilities with accessible toilets 2. Security challenges due to poor lighting 3. Poor solid waste collection and management 4. Poor drainage leading to occasional flooding 5. Inadequate water supply 6. Unreliable power supply 7. Poor town planning
In order to respond to some of these challenges, the change project was designed with the following objectives: Improved solid waste management system and sanitation within the market and along Nyando River. This intervention sought to develop a new solid waste management system aimed at reducing the volumes to landfill as much as possible. This would reduce the over dependence on the truck collection facilitated by the county government to the landfill in Kisumu. The system would consist of consists: 1. Material Recovery Facility (MRF) which is a four chamber facility for storage of recyclable waste, located at or close to the market and targeting primarily market waste 2. Training of environmental champions on waste management, particularly composting and recycling.
At the end of the programme, the material recovery facility had been completed. Further 30 champions were trained on organic composting and solid waste management. Small initiatives have started organic composting through the champions. Since it targeted behavioral change, its mostly practiced within homes. At least three homes can be shared as best practice and with several practical sessions and demonstrations taking place in those homes. Waste officers recruited under the project have been incorporated under the market management committee since most of them are businesspeople, weekly clean ups were organized with voluntary participation. They formed later a CBO after pooling together and used the same this far to negotiate with the county, almost being licensed as private waste collectors a replication of what happens in the main City. In conclusion a dedicated waste truck for collection of refuse has been set aside.
Improved access for all to recreational facilities and green spaces This intervention entailed educating the public on sustainable waste management through a sensitization and awareness creation program. This included implementation of three clean up exercises including procurement of tools (rakes, gloves, masks, etc.) and design and production Information Education and Communication materials such as flyers, T-shirts, banners and general public awareness. As at the reporting period residents of Ahero have participated in four clean up exercises using the assorted tools procured through the change project. In addition, the Nyando River MultiPark located along the river would have an assortment of tree species planted within and around it. The park would serve as a meeting place, accessible and available for all, and equipped with gentle lighting and park benches. Further an Eco Convenience Center would be set up inside the River Park to provide visitors and traders with basic amenities including safe and clean washrooms for men and women. Additionally, assorted tree would also be planted in public ground including schools. As at the programme the 5,500 assorted trees had been planted within the schools with a survival rate of between 7080% , public benches installed in the park as well as the construction of public toilets.
